title: Crown, wisdom, understanding
hookLine: Keter, Chochmah, Binah: will, the flash of an idea, and its unfolding
last: TEN LIGHTS, ONE GOD: THE SEFIROT.

cards: In the shower, on a walk, halfway through washing a pan: the idea arrives. All at once, whole, before you have words for it. Then comes the long part.

You sit down and work it out, piece by piece, until the flash becomes a plan someone else could follow. And underneath both, before either, there was something quieter: the wanting to solve it in the first place.
Kabbalists saw those three moments at the very top of the ten lights.

teach.b: Keter, Chochmah, Binah: crown, wisdom, understanding. First, the crown. A crown sits above the head, not inside it.
Kabbalists place Keter above thought and link it to will, the deep wanting that comes before any idea. Some teachers say so little can be said of it that it borders on Ein Sof itself.
Second, wisdom, Chochmah: the flash, a point of light before it has length or width. The book of Job asks, "But where shall wisdom be found?"
In Hebrew the word for where can also be read as from nothing, and kabbalists heard Job saying that wisdom comes from nothing: out of the hidden crown, a sudden point.

Third, understanding, Binah: the unfolding. Binah takes the point and gives it room, corridors and details, the way a seed becomes a plant. Kabbalists picture the two as a pair, a father and a mother.
The flash needs the unfolding, or it stays a spark. The unfolding needs the flash, or it has nothing to build. Fourth, where the three words meet.
When the Torah introduces Bezalel, the craftsman you met joining letters, God fills him "with the spirit of God, in wisdom, and in understanding, and in knowledge."
In Hebrew: chochmah, binah, da'at, the three words one Hasidic school, Chabad, took as its name.

Look back across this week: reason serving faith, the received tradition, the careful doorway, the letters, the One without end, the ten lights, and now the top three. A week spent climbing to the crown.

how: In Kabbalah, Keter, Chochmah and Binah are taught as the highest sefirot; Chabad Hasidism takes its name from Chochmah, Binah and Da'at, and its teaching applies them to how a person thinks.

o: the lowest of the ten lights, closest to the world
Keter: the will above thought, top of the ten lights

games.q: an idea flashes into your head, whole, before you have words for it. in this picture, what does it need next?
games.why: Chochmah, the flash, needs Binah, the unfolding, or it stays a spark. kabbalists picture them as a pair.

practice: Hold one small, real question in front of you, what to cook tonight or how to begin a task, and wait for an answer the way you'd wait for a bird to land.
When something arrives, notice the moment before it had words, then let it unfold slowly into one plain sentence. If nothing comes, notice the wanting underneath, and rest there.

wordCard.voice: Crown. Keter, the top of the ten lights: the will that sits above thought, before wisdom flashes and understanding unfolds. Today's word.

orig.note: Hebrew: crown. The highest of the ten sefirot, linked to will.

carryVoice: Your line: the flash and the unfolding. And before both, the wanting. Back tomorrow, same hill.
